stories.title: Millages for Detroit Zoo, Museum of African American History, Detroit Historical Society on ballot
stories.summary: Voters in Wayne and Oakland counties will decide on a new millage for the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History and the Detroit Historical Society, which would enable free admission and expanded outreach. A separate millage renewal for the Detroit Zoo, supporting a third of its operating budget, is also on the ballot for voters in Wayne, Oakland, and Macomb counties.

inputFacts.title: Millages for Detroit Zoo, Museum of African American History, Detroit Historical Society on ballot
inputFacts.summary: Voters in Oakland, Macomb, and Wayne counties will decide on a millage renewal for the Detroit Zoo and first-ever millage requests for the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History and Detroit Historical Society. The zoo seeks to maintain operations and educational programs, while the museums aim to expand free admission and outreach. Failure to pass could force budget cuts and reduced services.

stories.title: City Commission Grapples with Density Issues
stories.summary: Plymouth City Commission is pursuing an "expanded approach" to a new Residential Compatibility Ordinance, aiming to modernize and consolidate zoning regulations. This involves a comprehensive review of existing residential zoning before drafting new compatibility tools, with the goal of maintaining neighborhood context. No vote on the ordinance or expenditures has occurred yet.

inputFacts.title: City Commission Grapples with Density Issues
inputFacts.summary: The City Commission introduced a proposed Residential Compatibility Ordinance on September 21, 2026, aiming to modernize zoning regulations. The ordinance would address residential neighborhood compatibility through two approaches: a focused method on existing residential contexts or an expanded evaluation of current zoning rules. The Commission opted for a comprehensive review using the expanded approach but has not yet approved expenditures or finalized the ordinance.

inputFacts.title: Michigan voters can request absentee ballots for November election
inputFacts.summary: Michigan voters who receive absentee ballots but change their minds can spoil them at their local clerk's office until 4 p.m. on the Monday before Election Day (Nov. 2). Ballots can also be surrendered in person at polling places or early voting sites. If lost or not received, voters can sign a statement at their polling place to vote in person after verification with local clerks.

inputFacts.title: Support Student Radio During 88.1 The Park’s Thanks for Giving Pledge Drive, November 2–7
inputFacts.summary: 88.1 The Park, a student-run radio station in Plymouth and Canton, MI, is hosting a six-day pledge drive from November 2–7, 2026, to support its student broadcasters and programming. The station provides hands-on experience in broadcasting, journalism, and business, with alumni like Dave Snyder crediting their success to their time at WSDP. Donations will fund training, equipment, and resources for local news, sports coverage, and music programming.

inputFacts.title: Abdul El-Sayeds Democratic rival Haley Stevens endorses Gops Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate race
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Democrat Haley Stevens, former opponent of Abdul El-Sayed in the U.S. Senate primary, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers days before the election. The endorsement followed her exclusion from a joint campaign event with El-Sayed and caused shock within Democratic ranks. Stevens attended a Detroit church service with Rogers, while El-Sayed campaigned separately with other Democrats.

inputFacts.title: Haley Stevens endorses GOP candidate in Michigan Senate race, spurning Abdul El-Sayed
inputFacts.summary: Rep. Haley Stevens endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers instead of working with Abdul El-Sayed, whom she lost the Democratic primary to. The decision sparked criticism from Michigan Democratic Party Chair Curtis Hertel and highlighted internal party divisions over Israel-related rhetoric that could impact the 2028 presidential race.

inputFacts.title: ‘Heart dropping’: Bride says Metro Detroit mobile bartender won’t refund after selling business
inputFacts.summary: Brides in Metro Detroit report being ghosted by Sip of Eden, a mobile bartending service, after paying deposits. The service was sold to Bartenders Elite, but the new owner refuses refunds, claiming he was also scammed. Bride Allison Blue and others are struggling to recover their payments.

inputFacts.title: What happens if you make a mistake on your Michigan ballot?
inputFacts.summary: Michigan voters may have questions about ballot mistakes and election procedures as the 2026 midterms approach. The article explains straight-party voting rules, overvote handling, and correction processes for in-person and absentee ballots.
